title: Nvidia’s Efforts to Influence US AI Chip Export Policy Strain Ties With Washington
summary:
Nvidia is facing a decline in credibility among U.S. policymakers over its efforts to secure looser export controls on AI chips bound for China. Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, stated that the chipmaker created mistrust in Washington by exaggerating the technical capabilities of China's domestic AI hardware. This friction comes as congressional patience wanes and debates over chip restrictions are set to resume.

The company's influence campaign included funding the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) and coordinating on policy reports that were not labeled as sponsored. Nvidia also leveraged its relationship with OpenAI, which may have softened its opposition to China exports to avoid upsetting CEO Jensen Huang and to protect a deal in which Nvidia guaranteed more than $100 billion in leases for OpenAI’s Ohio data center. While OpenAI has historically avoided challenging Nvidia's sales to China, the firm has more recently explicitly endorsed certain export controls.

selectedTweets.text:
full story not yet been told - "Nvidia tangled with think tanks before Trump’s return to the White House. In 2023, several people familiar with the discussions said Nvidia had tried to use its influence—including funding—to sideline Greg Allen, then director of the AI policy arm of the Center for Strategic and International Studies, an influential think tank focused on national security and geopolitics. Allen staunchly supports chip export controls.

One of those people said Nvidia became a major donor to CSIS and coordinated with the think tank on specific policy reports not labeled as sponsored. CSIS did not ultimately fire Allen; he left the think tank earlier this year. "
